text: All tests pass. The fix was a one-character change: the greedy packing condition used `< width` instead of `<= width`, so a word that would make the line exactly `width` long was incorrectly pushed to the next line. Now `wrap("aaa bbb", 7)` returns `["aaa bbb"]` as expected, and overlong-word splitting is unaffected.

arguments.summary: Fixed off-by-one in wrapper/wrap.py: changed the greedy packing condition from `len(current) + 1 + len(word) < width` to `<= width` so a word that exactly fills the line stays on it (e.g., wrap("aaa bbb", 7) -> ["aaa bbb"]). All tests pass.
